quizzes.title: Spell It Right
quizzes.description: Tricky spellings, plurals and the building blocks of English grammar.

questions.q: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.note: A handy memory aid: one Collar and two Sleeves.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'mouse' when talking about the animal?
questions.note: The same pattern turns 'louse' into 'lice'.

questions.q: The five-letter word 'queue' contains four vowels.
questions.note: Remove the last four letters and it still sounds the same: 'Q'.

questions.q: What is the opposite of 'ancient'?
questions.note: 'Old', 'antique' and 'historic' are all close in meaning to 'ancient'.

questions.q: How many letters are there in the English alphabet?
questions.note: Accept 'twenty-six'; E is the most commonly used letter in English.

questions.q: Which word is the verb in 'The cat sleeps on the mat'?
questions.note: Verbs are often called 'doing words'.

questions.q: An adjective is a word used to describe an action.
questions.note: Adjectives describe nouns; words that tell us how an action is done are adverbs.

questions.q: Which of these words means the same as 'happy'?
questions.note: Words with the same meaning are called synonyms.

questions.q: What is the past tense of the verb 'go'?
questions.note: 'Went' was originally the past tense of the old verb 'wend'.

questions.q: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.note: Remember: there's 'a rat' in sep-a-r-ate.

quizzes.title: Where Words Come From
quizzes.description: Everyday English words with surprising roots in other languages and real people.

questions.q: The German word 'kindergarten' literally means what?
questions.note: Friedrich Fröbel coined the term for his early-years school in 1840.

questions.q: The word 'robot' was introduced in a 1920 play by which Czech writer?
questions.note: Accept 'Čapek' or 'Capek'; the play was R.U.R., and the word came from 'robota', forced labour.

questions.q: The word 'shampoo' comes into English from which language?
questions.note: It comes from 'chāmpo', meaning to press or massage.

questions.q: 'Quarantine' comes from the Italian for how many days?
questions.note: Ships arriving in Venice during plague outbreaks were kept isolated for 40 days.

questions.q: The word 'tsunami' comes from Japanese words meaning 'harbour wave'.
questions.note: In Japanese, 'tsu' means harbour and 'nami' means wave.

questions.q: The word 'muscle' comes from a Latin word meaning what?
questions.note: A flexing muscle was thought to look like a mouse moving under the skin.

questions.q: The verb 'to boycott' is named after Charles Boycott. Who was he?
questions.note: In 1880, his neighbours in County Mayo refused to have any dealings with him.

questions.q: The word 'algebra' comes from Greek.
questions.note: It comes from Arabic 'al-jabr', from a 9th-century book by al-Khwarizmi.

questions.q: The word 'disaster' comes from Italian and literally means 'bad ___'. Fill in the gap.
questions.note: It reflects the old belief that the stars and planets shaped people's fate.

questions.q: The word 'safari' comes from Swahili. What does it mean?
questions.note: Swahili borrowed it from the Arabic 'safar', also meaning journey.

quizzes.title: Say What? Idioms
quizzes.description: Colourful everyday phrases that mean something very different from what they say.

questions.q: If something 'costs an arm and a leg', it is…
questions.note: A similar phrase is 'to cost a fortune'.

questions.q: What does it mean to 'let the cat out of the bag'?
questions.note: A close relative is 'to spill the beans'.

questions.q: To 'bite the bullet' means to face something unpleasant with courage.
questions.note: It is used when accepting something difficult that cannot be avoided.

questions.q: Complete the proverb: 'Don't count your ___ before they hatch.'
questions.note: It warns against relying on something good before it has actually happened.

questions.q: Someone who is 'under the weather' is…
questions.note: It usually means mildly ill rather than seriously ill.

questions.q: What does 'once in a blue moon' mean?
questions.note: In one modern sense, a blue moon is the second full moon in a calendar month.

questions.q: Actors say 'break a leg' to wish each other bad luck.
questions.note: It means good luck; saying 'good luck' backstage is traditionally thought to be unlucky.

questions.q: In a mystery story, what is a 'red herring'?
questions.note: A real red herring is a strong-smelling smoked fish.

questions.q: Complete the idiom for a heavy downpour: 'It's raining cats and ___.'
questions.note: Its origin is uncertain; no single explanation is widely accepted.

questions.q: If you 'hit the nail on the head', you…
questions.note: Another way to say it is 'spot on'.

quizzes.title: Tongues of the World
quizzes.description: Scripts, speakers and surprising facts about the languages people speak around the globe.

questions.q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.note: Spanish is second for native speakers; English has the most speakers in total.

questions.q: What is the official language of Brazil?
questions.note: Brazil has more Portuguese speakers than all other countries combined.

questions.q: Basque, spoken in parts of Spain and France, is not related to any other living language.
questions.note: Linguists call a language like this a 'language isolate'.

questions.q: How many official languages does the United Nations have?
questions.note: They are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.

questions.q: Which country has the most living languages, with more than 800?
questions.note: Accept 'PNG'; it has around 840 living languages.

questions.q: The Cyrillic alphabet is used to write which of these languages?
questions.note: The alphabet is named in honour of Saint Cyril, a 9th-century Byzantine missionary.

questions.q: Which of these languages is written from right to left?
questions.note: Arabic, Persian and Urdu are also written from right to left.

questions.q: Japanese is written using just one writing system.
questions.note: Japanese mixes kanji with two syllabaries, hiragana and katakana.

questions.q: In which ancient language were the Vedas composed?
questions.note: Accept 'Vedic Sanskrit'; the Rigveda is one of the oldest Indo-European texts.

questions.q: Besides hieroglyphs and Demotic, the Rosetta Stone carries text in which language?
questions.note: Jean-François Champollion announced his decipherment of hieroglyphs in 1822.
